tribe: Banu Kalb of Quda'a — client of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
era: The Beloved — the only companion named in the Qur'an
teaser: He was carried off as a boy and sold for four hundred dirhams. His name is in the Book of Allah.
quran_mention: «فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِنْهَا وَطَرًا زَوَّجْنَاكَهَا» — 'So when Zayd had accomplished his desire from her, We gave her to you in marriage' (33:37). No other companion is named by name in the Qur'an.

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: Taken on a visit to his mother's family
layers.content:
Zayd ibn Harithah was of Kalb, of Quda'a, and his mother was Su'da bint Tha'laba of the Banu Ma'n of Tayy. She took him with her to visit her own people. Horsemen of the Banu al-Qayn ibn Jasr raided past those houses and carried the boy away. Ibn Sa'd says he was young enough to be useful as a servant and no older. They brought him to the market at Ukaz and put him up for sale.

Hakim ibn Hizam bought him for four hundred dirhams as a gift for his aunt, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. When Khadijah married Muhammad ﷺ she gave the boy to him.

His father did not know any of this. Harithah composed a lament that Ibn Sa'd preserves in full — 'I weep for Zayd, not knowing what has happened to him. Is he alive and hoped for, or has his fate taken him? By Allah, I do not know, even if I ask, whether the plains or the mountains have destroyed you.' He said he would wear out red camels searching the earth for his son until his own death came.

Usama's report gives the physical description: ten years younger than the Prophet ﷺ, a short man, very dark-skinned, with a flat nose. His kunya came from his son: Abu Usama.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (from Hisham ibn Muhammad al-Kalbi and from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Usama)

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Offered his family back, and he refused
layers.content:
Some Kalbis came on Hajj and recognised him. He gave them verses to carry home: tell my people I am living at the House and the stations of the Hajj, stop wearing out your camels, praise be to Allah, I am in the best of families. His father heard it and said, 'My son, by the Lord of the Ka'bah.'

Harithah and his brother Ka'b came to Makkah with ransom money. They found him in the mosque and appealed to his lineage — son of Abdullah, son of Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim, you are the people of the Haram, you help those in distress and feed captives. We have come about our son. Name the ransom.

The answer was not a price. 'Let him choose. If he chooses you, he is yours without ransom. If he chooses me, by Allah, I am not one to impose a choice on anyone who chose me.'

Zayd was called. Do you know these men. Yes — this is my father and this is my uncle. Then choose. He said, 'I am not one who would ever choose someone over you. You are like a father and a mother to me.' They were appalled: you would choose slavery over freedom, over your father and your house. 'Yes. I have seen something from this man because of which I would never choose anyone over him.'

The Prophet ﷺ took him to the Hijr: 'Whoever is present, bear witness that Zayd is my son. I inherit from him and he from me.' Az-Zuhri held that Zayd was the first person to accept Islam.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III (Hisham al-Kalbi from his father and Jamil ibn Marthad at-Ta'i; az-Zuhri on his precedence)

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: Never sent out except in command
layers.content:
Usama's narration of what his father was told is short and hard to read without stopping: 'Zayd, you are our client, and you are from me and to me, and the person I love the most.' In the narration concerning Hamzah he is also recorded being told, 'You are our brother and our client.'

When the brotherhood pairs were made, Zayd was joined with Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle, and with Usayd ibn Hudayr of the Ansar. On the morning of Uhud, Hamzah made him the executor of his estate.

He emigrated to Madinah and stayed with Kulthum ibn al-Hidm, or with Sa'd ibn Khaythama — the reports differ. He was at Badr and Uhud, at the Ditch, at Hudaybiyah and at Khaybar, and he is counted among the archers. When the Prophet ﷺ went out to al-Muraysi' he left Zayd in charge of Madinah.

He commanded seven expeditions. The first was al-Qarada, where he captured a caravan; Abu Sufyan and the important men escaped, Furat ibn Hayyan was taken, and the goods were brought back for the fifth to be set aside. Salama ibn al-Akwa said he went out seven times under the Prophet ﷺ and seven times under Zayd.

Aisha put it plainly: the Messenger of Allah never sent Zayd out in an army without putting him in command of it.
layers.hadith_ref: Narrated by Usama ibn Zayd; and by Aisha on his command of every expedition — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: The Qur'an gave him his name and took away his title
layers.content:
For years people in Madinah called him Zayd ibn Muhammad. Abdullah ibn Umar said so directly: we used to call him Zayd ibn Muhammad until the Qur'an came down.

His marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, the Prophet's own cousin, did not hold. Zayd intended divorce. The Prophet ﷺ urged him to keep her — and the ayah that came down about that moment quotes the Prophet's words to him and names him: to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour and on whom you too had bestowed favour, you said, keep your wife and fear Allah. Then, after the divorce and the waiting period, the same ayah records the marriage in the first person: so when Zayd had accomplished his desire from her, We gave her to you in marriage — so that there would be no difficulty for the believers regarding the wives of adopted sons.

And with the same revelation the adoption itself was dissolved. Call them by the names of their fathers, that is more just with Allah. Muhammad is not the father of any man among you. From that day he was Zayd ibn Harithah again, and al-Miqdad, who had been called ibn al-Aswad, went back to ibn Amr.

Sit with the size of that. His private failed marriage became scripture. He lost the most honoured name in Arabia. And when the Prophet ﷺ next spoke of him it was still 'you are from me and to me.'
layers.quran_ref: Quran 33:37; and Quran 33:5 — 'Call them by the names of their fathers, that is more just with Allah'; and Quran 33:40 — 'Muhammad is not the father of any man among you'
layers.hadith_ref: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: 'We used to call him Zayd ibn Muhammad until the Qur'an was revealed' — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III (Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn Umar, Ali ibn Husayn, Thabit); al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: He entered the Garden running
layers.content:
At Mu'tah the Prophet ﷺ put him in charge of the army and placed him ahead of the commanders — ahead of his own cousin Ja'far and ahead of Abdullah ibn Rawahah. When the two sides met, the commanders fought on foot. Zayd took the banner and the people fought with him, and he was killed by a spear thrust while the Muslims were still in their rows. Mu'tah was in Jumada al-Ula of the eighth year. He was fifty-five.

The Prophet ﷺ prayed over him and said, 'Ask forgiveness for him. He entered the Garden running.' When the news of the three came, he stood and began with Zayd, and asked forgiveness for him three times before naming the other two.

Then he went to the family. Zayd's daughter wept in front of him and he wept until he was sobbing. Sa'd ibn Ubadah asked him what this was. He said: this is the yearning of the lover for the beloved.

What the ummah kept from him is not a rank or a conquest. It is a proof about worth. A boy stolen from a caravan road and sold for the price of a few camels was made the commander of Quraysh's nobles, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the one name from among all the companions that Muslims will recite in prayer until the end of the world. His son Usama, may Allah be pleased with them both, would later be given command over men older than himself.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Ask forgiveness for him. He entered the Garden running' — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III (Muhammad ibn Umar; Abu Maysara; Khalid ibn Shumayr)

quiz.prompt: How did Zayd come into the Prophet's household?

options.text: He was born into it
Khadijah gave him to the Prophet ﷺ when they married, having received him as a gift
Abu Talib bought him
He was captured in a battle

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — from Hisham ibn Muhammad al-Kalbi
quiz.scholar_reflection: Hakim ibn Hizam bought him at the Ukaz market for four hundred dirhams as a gift for his aunt Khadijah. She then gave him to her husband.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ offer when Zayd's father and uncle came with ransom money?

options.text: He named a price and they paid it
He refused to see them
He let Zayd choose — free without ransom if he chose them
He asked Khadijah to decide

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — from Hisham al-Kalbi and Jamil ibn Marthad at-Ta'i
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'If he chooses you, then he is yours without ransom. If he chooses me, by Allah, I am not the one to impose a choice over anyone who chose me.' Zayd chose to stay.

quiz.prompt: Which surah names Zayd, and what does it record?

options.text: Surah al-Ahzab (33:37), recording his divorce and the marriage that followed
Surah at-Tawbah, recording his migration
Surah al-Fath, recording the pledge under the tree
Surah an-Nahl, recording his martyrdom

quiz.citation: Quran 33:37; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar; Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He is the only companion the Qur'an names by name. The verse that honours him with that also records the failure of his marriage.

quiz.prompt: What did Aisha say about how the Prophet ﷺ deployed Zayd?

options.text: That he was never sent out without being put in command
That he was always kept behind in Madinah
That he was only sent as a messenger, never as a fighter
That he served under Khalid ibn al-Walid

quiz.citation: Narrated by Aisha through al-Bahi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He commanded seven expeditions, and at Mu'tah he was placed ahead of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. Salama ibn al-Akwa served under him seven times.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say after praying over Zayd's body?

options.text: That he would be raised with the prophets
'Ask forgiveness for him. He entered the Garden running.'
Nothing — he was silent
That the army should turn back at once

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — reported by Muhammad ibn Umar
quiz.scholar_reflection: Zayd was killed by a spear thrust at Mu'tah in Jumada al-Ula of year 8, aged fifty-five. When his daughter wept before the Prophet ﷺ he sobbed, and called it the yearning of the lover for the beloved.

quiz.prompt: Zayd chose the man he served over his own father and freedom. Would you know that kind of clarity if you had it?

options.text: Family comes first for me, and I would have gone home
I would want to be told what the right answer was
I have felt certainty like that once, about something
I do not trust my own certainty that much

quiz.citation: Reflection on the ransom narration, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'I have seen something from this man because of which I would never choose anyone over him.' Note that he was not asked to reject his father, only to choose. His father left happy.

quiz.prompt: His father spent years composing poetry to a son he thought was dead. What do you do with a loss you cannot resolve?

options.text: I keep looking long after it is reasonable
I make myself accept it and move
I put it into words, which is its own kind of searching
I avoid thinking about it directly

quiz.citation: Reflection on the lament of Harithah ibn Sharahil, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'I will make the fine reddish camels toil hard in the land, and neither the camels nor myself will tire of wandering — for my entire life, or until my death comes to me.' Then some pilgrims happened to recognise a face.

quiz.prompt: The Qur'an took away the name Zayd ibn Muhammad. How would you have received that?

options.text: As a demotion, and I would have felt it
As being handed back my real father's name
As a cost worth paying for a ruling the ummah needed
I honestly do not know, and that is the honest answer

quiz.citation: Reflection on Quran 33:5 and 33:40, and Abdullah ibn Umar's narration, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The ruling was general — al-Miqdad was returned to his own father's name in the same movement. And the Prophet ﷺ still called Zayd the person he loved most.

quiz.prompt: A boy sold at a market ended up commanding the nobles of Quraysh. What does that do to how you read status?

options.text: It tells me status is mostly accident of birth
It tells me Islam genuinely reordered who mattered
It tells me one man's decisions can reorder a society
I want to believe it and I am not sure my own world works that way

quiz.citation: Reflection on Zayd's command at Mu'tah, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Hamzah, uncle of the Prophet ﷺ and of Banu Hashim, made Zayd the executor of his estate. Ja'far feared being ranked above him. Neither of them treated it as strange.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ wept until he sobbed and called it the yearning of the lover for the beloved. What is your relationship with your own grief?

options.text: I hold it in, mostly out of habit
I let it out and feel exposed afterwards
I did not know this was allowed
I grieve alone and function in front of people

quiz.citation: Narrated by Khalid ibn Shumayr from Abdullah ibn Riyah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Sa'd ibn Ubadah asked the question many of us would have asked. The answer named the feeling instead of apologising for it. Tears were never the thing the Prophet ﷺ forbade.
